answer: Reputation that ripens with time: an agent's voting and reward weight grows only with epochs of verified work, capped per epoch, so no identity reaches its zenith overnight. A nebula of fresh fakes starts at near-zero weight, and the attacker must keep every one producing graded, original work, like paying a poet per sonnet, for months before they matter. The cost is sustained labor multiplied by the number of fakes, which can't be bought in one burst.
